key_insight: A foundation-model-based, data-efficient pipeline can detect duodenal epithelial neoplasia on whole-slide biopsy images with strong accuracy across hospitals.
clinical_relevance: This could help pathology teams screen rare duodenal lesions more consistently, even when local labelled data are limited.
method: H&E-stained duodenal biopsy WSIs from 5 hospitals were split into patches and encoded with the Hibou-B foundation model.
Patch embeddings were standardized using either global or site-specific unsupervised normalization, then reduced with PCA.
A Gaussian mixture model and Random Forest classifier were evaluated with leave-one-hospital-out cross-validation and an external test hospital.
evidence_signal: The study used 8,027 normal and 401 neoplastic biopsies; performance reached 90% mean accuracy in cross-validation and 94% accuracy on an independent external hospital set.
watch_item: Results are promising, but real-world deployment will still need prospective validation and careful checks for site-specific workflow differences.
paper_title: Data-efficient machine learning for the detection of duodenal neoplasia: a multi-centre study
